headline: Cotton Street outreach workers and litter help sent to city budget review.
summary: Staff proposed two more outreach workers and about a half-time public works position at the Cotton Street food site, plus roughly $10,000 for containers. The ideas now go to the Finance Committee for the budget process that starts in February. Speakers from the public gave mixed views, with some favoring an indoor site and others supporting the current work.
decisions: Referred Cotton Street outreach worker and litter requests to the Finance Committee for budget review, 3-0.
discussion: Cotton Street food site: Speakers disagreed about the site. One urged an indoor space downtown, saying outdoor feeding draws attention. Another said the current work has helped people move into permanent housing.

Homelessness task force charge: Members discussed narrowing the goals, measuring results, and adding partners such as a university and health providers. Some views supported including residents and businesses, while others warned about focusing on people who oppose services in their area.

Before and after care lottery: Staff plan to open registration for at least six weeks starting in April, then hold a lottery in mid-May. Spots would be held back for fee waivers and McKinney-Vento students.

Police staffing levels: The police chief reported 26 vacancies against 158 budgeted positions, with more officers on leave. The chief said close to 200 officers would be needed to meet the department's full needs.

decision_evidence.quote: So moved. Second. Moved by Councillor Palacier, seconded by Councillor McKnivich. Councillor Palacier, how do you vote? Yes. Councillor McKnivich. Yes. I'm a yes. We have voted to move this item to finance for consideration for the fiscal impact for the next budget year.
